source_excerpt:
Small Android apps built on Android Auto's own head unit mode:
PhoneAuto runs the full Android Auto car display on your phone's own screen, in portrait or landscape . It brings back the "Android Auto for phone screens" experience: big buttons, a driving dashboard, Maps, music, calls, messages and Google Assistant.
CarCast Launcher connects your phone's Android Auto to a CarCast receiver over Wi-Fi, with no cable.
TarPlay Tesla shows your phone's Android Auto in your Tesla's browser , over the phone's hotspot. No app on the car, no account.
All are free, with no ads, accounts or tracking.
Download · User guide · Report a problem · Release notes
This repository is for releases, documentation and issues . The source code is not public.
The short version is below. The user guide has every step, one-tap start, CarCast Launcher and troubleshooting.
Download the APK from Releases and open it on your phone. Allow installs from your browser or file manager when Android asks.
Install Android Auto from Google Play if your phone doesn't have it.
Turn on Android Auto developer mode (one time): Open Android Auto settings (Settings › Connected devices › Android Auto, or search "Android Auto"). Scroll down and tap Version 10 times, until it says developer mode is on. Tap the ⋮ menu › Start head unit server .
Open Android Auto settings (Settings › Connected devices › Android Auto, or search "Android Auto").
Scroll down and tap Version 10 times, until it says developer mode is on.
Tap the ⋮ menu › Start head unit server .
Open PhoneAuto, switch on Portrait mode if you want it, and tap Start Android Auto . Tap ✕ to end the session.
Open CarCast Launcher on a phone that's on the same Wi-Fi as your CarCast receiver. The receiver finds the phone and Android Auto appears on its screen.
Open TarPlay, turn on the phone's hotspot, connect the car to it ( Controls › Wi-Fi ), and tap Start . Then open https://v.tarplay.com:8081 in the Tesla browser. Details in the user guide .
The APK builds can start Android Auto's head unit server for you through an accessibility service. On Android 13 and later, sideloaded apps need restricted settings allowed first: Settings › Apps › PhoneAuto (or CarCast Launcher, TarPlay) › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings , then turn the app on under Settings › Accessibility. You can skip this and start the head unit server by hand.
The APKs here are beta builds that stop working on the date in the file name (e.g. PhoneAuto-beta-2027-01-19.apk ). Download a newer release before then.
They are signed with a different key from the Google Play versions, so you can't update between them. Uninstall one before installing the other.
Is it safe? Nothing leaves your phone. PhoneAuto talks to Android Auto on the same phone (127.0.0.1); CarCast Launcher only talks to devices on your own Wi-Fi; TarPlay Tesla only to the car on your phone's hotspot (it fetches the v.tarplay.com certificate from the internet). Privacy policies: PhoneAuto · CarCast Launcher .
"Start head unit server" is missing. Developer mode isn't on yet. Keep tapping Version in Android Auto settings until it says developer mode is enabled.
It's stuck on "connecting". In Android Auto settings › ⋮, tap Stop head unit server , then Start head unit server , and reopen the app.
Do I need to start the server every time? Usually only after a phone restart or an Android Auto update.
Open an issue with your phone model, Android version and Android Auto version (Android Auto settings › Version).
